_spec.purpose: A standalone web edition of the archived visual story.
_spec.law: Facts resolve to the original verified claim record. A layout rebuild does not reverify reporting.

dek.text: The FAA takes comment until {{date:c2}} on a draft that assesses letting Zipline fly delivery drones over five Texas metros. In it, a pod on a line judges the drop spot itself.

introduction.text: Zipline International is [seeking FAA approval to begin commercial package delivery operations in five Texas metropolitan areas](c1). The five are Amarillo, Austin, El Paso, Houston and San Antonio. The Federal Aviation Administration has published a draft environmental assessment of that request and [takes comments on it until {{date:c2}}](c2).

The document is a draft, and it says who prepared it. [Zipline prepared this draft environmental assessment (draft EA) under the supervision of the FAA](c6). The agency says [all substantive comments received will be responded to in the final EA](c5), so the final assessment and the decision it informs are still to come.

paragraphs.text: At a delivery the aircraft stays in the air. The draft has it [generally operated at an altitude of 330 feet above ground level](c11), and in the delivery sequence it [holds a hover at 330 feet AGL](c19) while the pod goes down to the ground and back. The draft puts that hover at about 75 seconds.
The pod does the deciding. The draft says [the pod automatically controls its position laterally and evaluates the delivery location](c17), and that it continues to descend if the location is clear.

[If the pod is unable to automatically identify the delivery target and evaluate its suitability, an image is sent to an operator for real-time evaluation](c18). The draft gives no figure for how often that happens. The sentence sits in its section on visual effects rather than in its description of flight operations. People appear elsewhere in the draft too. It says [the Remote Pilot in Command has the ability to command flight termination](c33) if an aircraft flies outside its operating area.

Routing is automated too. [Routes are generated by software that takes into consideration factors including weather risk, wind direction, and population density](c15), and the aircraft [automatically deconflict with each other](c16). The draft describes the aircraft itself as [highly automated](c12).

The draft's table sets a ceiling for each metro. [Across the five metros the totals are 220 Chargers, 4,400 Dropboxes and 220,000 deliveries a day](c7), and every delivery counts as [three transits](c8). A Charger is a site rather than a single mast, since [most Chargers would have around 36 docks](c32). Houston and San Antonio carry the largest allotments. Operations would run [24 hours a day, 7 days per week, including holidays](c9), with [approximately 95% of flights](c10) between 7 am and 10 pm.

Those numbers are maximums the draft assesses, not deliveries anyone has flown. The draft itself says [there would be variability in the actual number of flights per day based on customer demand and weather conditions](c24).

sections.heading: Noise, as the draft measures it

paragraphs.text: The draft applies the FAA's own test, under which [noise impacts would be significant if the action would increase the DNL by 1.5 dB or more for a noise sensitive area that is exposed to noise at or above DNL 65 dB](c20). At [400 average daily deliveries per day](c21) it puts delivery noise at no more than DNL 58.1 dB at any distance from a delivery point, and says it [would not exceed DNL 59.7 dB at any point](c21). The draft calls 59.7 dB [the DNL threshold below which increases of 1.5 dB or more in aviation noise cannot result in significant impacts](c35). The draft adds that [deliveries to single family homes would be much lower, so this maximum represents delivery locations such as a large apartment complex](c29).
It concludes that [the proposed action would not have a significant noise impact](c26). Its noise estimates rest on [sound level testing data collected by Zipline](c27).

sections.heading: What this edition does not establish

paragraphs.text: The draft does not say how often a pod sends an image to an operator, or what share of deliveries that would be, and this edition publishes no estimate of either. It does not establish that any of the ceilings would be reached. The configuration of the aircraft in the visual edition is illustrative between the dimensions the draft gives.
